I had $0 in my bank account when I decided to quit my job.

That one line pulls you in immediately, and that's exactly the point.

When I was teaching content hooks the other day, the pattern I kept seeing was people starting their posts by explaining everything before they say anything interesting. They give you the timeline, the background, the context, and by the time they get to the actual moment that matters, you've already scrolled.

The best storytellers skip all that and open at the most interesting moment, with stakes already baked into the first sentence.

"I had $0 in my bank account when I decided to quit my job" works because the tension is right there on the first read. You feel the weight of it, and your brain immediately wants to know what happened next.

The weak version of that same story sounds something like, "For a while I'd been unhappy at work, my coworker said something, my manager didn't back me up, and eventually I just decided to leave." Same experience, completely different pull. One makes you lean in, one gives you a reason to keep scrolling past.

There's a concept called the curiosity gap, which is the distance between what your audience already knows and what they want to know. A strong hook opens that gap honestly, and a good story closes it. That's the whole thing.

If your content isn't getting the traction you want, go back and read your opening line out loud. If there are no stakes in it, your audience has nothing to be curious about yet.

I use to have a very unhealthy relationship with alcohol. I drank to numb and to avoid myself, my emotions and my calling. Last year I took a year off from drinking and did some extensive traveling and really dove deeper on healing myself and my relationship with some of my unhealthy habits. 

I learned that everything we do is for a reason and a “payoff” whether it’s causing chaos, scrolling socials or drinking too much we are looking to avoid something we aren’t ready to acknowledge. In the year of sobriety I peeled back the layers of myself and really saw who I was and what I was trying to run from. 

Now I can have some drinks with my boys or when I go on a date as a social connection rather than automatic crutch. I’m fully living in my calling doing the work that I was meant to do. When I was playing small living below my potential the alc helped me distract myself from the fact I wasn’t living a life that I was suppose to live.

I wanted to share this story. If this was for you I’m glad it made it to you. 🙏
